cards.front: In SLE, which autoantibody is the best screening test, which are the most specific, and which follows disease activity?
cards.back: **ANA**: very sensitive but not specific, so it is the screening test. **Anti-dsDNA** and **anti-Smith**: highly specific. **Anti-dsDNA** levels rise with disease activity and **lupus nephritis**, often together with **low C3 and C4**.
cards.back_pt: **FAN** (ANA): muito sensível, mas pouco específico; é o teste de triagem. **Anti-dsDNA** e **anti-Sm**: altamente específicos. O **anti-dsDNA** sobe com a atividade da doença e a **nefrite lúpica**, muitas vezes com **C3 e C4 baixos**.

cards.front: Which antibody marks drug-induced lupus, and how does the disease differ from SLE?
cards.back: **Anti-histone** antibodies. Classic drugs: **hydralazine**, **procainamide** and **isoniazid**. The kidneys and CNS are usually spared, anti-dsDNA is usually negative, and symptoms **resolve after the drug is stopped**.
cards.back_pt: Anticorpos **anti-histona**. Fármacos clássicos: **hidralazina**, **procainamida** e **isoniazida**. Rins e SNC geralmente são poupados, o anti-dsDNA costuma ser negativo e os sintomas **regridem após a suspensão do fármaco**.

cards.front: What are the core features of Sjögren syndrome, and what is its main cancer risk?
cards.back: Lymphocytes infiltrate and damage the **lacrimal and salivary glands**: dry eyes (**keratoconjunctivitis sicca**), dry mouth, dental caries and parotid swelling. Antibodies: **anti-Ro (SSA)** and **anti-La (SSB)**. Main cancer risk: **marginal zone (MALT) B-cell lymphoma**.
cards.back_pt: Linfócitos infiltram e lesam as **glândulas lacrimais e salivares**: olho seco (**ceratoconjuntivite seca**), boca seca, cáries e aumento das parótidas. Anticorpos: **anti-Ro (SSA)** e **anti-La (SSB)**. Principal risco de câncer: **linfoma B da zona marginal (MALT)**.

cards.front: How do limited and diffuse systemic sclerosis differ in antibody and organ risk?
cards.back: **Limited (CREST)**: skin of the face and distal limbs; **anti-centromere**; late **pulmonary arterial hypertension**. **Diffuse**: skin also of the trunk and proximal limbs; **anti-Scl-70** (topoisomerase I); early **interstitial lung disease** and **scleroderma renal crisis**.
cards.back_pt: **Limitada (CREST)**: pele da face e da parte distal dos membros; **anticentrômero**; **hipertensão arterial pulmonar** tardia. **Difusa**: pele também do tronco e da parte proximal dos membros; **anti-Scl-70** (topoisomerase I); **doença pulmonar intersticial** precoce e **crise renal esclerodérmica**.

cards.front: How do dermatomyositis and polymyositis differ?
cards.back: Both: symmetric **proximal weakness**, high **CK**, possible **anti-Jo-1**. **Dermatomyositis**: **heliotrope rash**, **Gottron papules**, **perimysial** inflammation with perifascicular atrophy, and a link to **occult cancer**. **Polymyositis**: no rash; **endomysial CD8+ T cells**.
cards.back_pt: Ambas: **fraqueza proximal** simétrica, **CK** elevada, possível **anti-Jo-1**. **Dermatomiosite**: **eritema em heliotropo**, **pápulas de Gottron**, inflamação **perimisial** com atrofia perifascicular e associação com **câncer oculto**. **Polimiosite**: sem lesões de pele; **linfócitos T CD8+ endomisiais**.

cards.front: Which antibody defines mixed connective tissue disease, and what does the disease look like?
cards.back: High titers of **anti-U1 RNP** antibodies. The patient has overlapping features of **SLE**, **systemic sclerosis** and **polymyositis**, typically with **Raynaud phenomenon** and swollen, puffy hands.
cards.back_pt: Títulos altos de anticorpos **anti-U1 RNP**. O paciente tem características sobrepostas de **LES**, **esclerose sistêmica** e **polimiosite**, tipicamente com **fenômeno de Raynaud** e mãos edemaciadas (*puffy hands*).

cards.front: How do polymyalgia rheumatica and fibromyalgia differ?
cards.back: **Polymyalgia rheumatica**: over age 50; pain and morning stiffness of the **shoulders and hips**; high **ESR/CRP**; normal CK and strength; linked to **giant cell arteritis**; fast response to low-dose steroids. **Fibromyalgia**: widespread pain, fatigue, poor sleep; **normal labs**.
cards.back_pt: **Polimialgia reumática**: acima de 50 anos; dor e rigidez matinal em **ombros e quadris**; **VHS/PCR** elevadas; CK e força normais; associada à **arterite de células gigantes**; resposta rápida a corticoide em dose baixa. **Fibromialgia**: dor difusa, fadiga, sono ruim; **exames normais**.

cards.front: What are the key features of Behçet disease?
cards.back: A **variable-vessel vasculitis**, most common along the old Silk Road (e.g., Turkey). Recurrent painful **oral and genital ulcers**, **uveitis**, skin lesions (erythema nodosum, **pathergy**) and venous or arterial thrombosis. Linked to **HLA-B51**.
cards.back_pt: Uma **vasculite de vasos variáveis**, mais comum ao longo da antiga Rota da Seda (ex.: Turquia). **Úlceras orais e genitais** dolorosas e recorrentes, **uveíte**, lesões de pele (eritema nodoso, **patergia**) e trombose venosa ou arterial. Associada ao **HLA-B51**.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman has had 10 months of tight, thick skin. It began on her fingers and has spread to her forearms, upper arms, chest and face. Her fingers turn white and then blue in the cold. She has a dry cough and shortness of breath on exertion, and fine crackles are heard at both lung bases. Today she has a severe headache. Blood pressure is 196/112 mm Hg; it was 124/78 mm Hg 3 months ago. Serum creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL; it was 0.8 mg/dL 3 months ago. A blood smear shows schistocytes. Which autoantibody is most likely present?
questions.explanation: Skin thickening that reaches the upper arms and chest, with **interstitial lung disease**, is **diffuse systemic sclerosis**. Sudden severe hypertension, rising creatinine and schistocytes are **scleroderma renal crisis**, which is treated with an ACE inhibitor. Diffuse disease is linked to **anti-Scl-70** (anti-RNA polymerase III is also linked to renal crisis). Anti-centromere goes with **limited** disease (CREST), where the skin change stays distal and the typical late problem is pulmonary arterial hypertension, not renal crisis. High-dose glucocorticoids can trigger renal crisis.
questions.explanation_pt: Espessamento da pele que atinge braços e tórax, com **doença pulmonar intersticial**, é **esclerose sistêmica difusa**. Hipertensão grave de início súbito, creatinina em elevação e esquizócitos indicam **crise renal esclerodérmica**, tratada com IECA. A forma difusa associa-se ao **anti-Scl-70** (o anti-RNA polimerase III também se associa à crise renal). O anticentrômero acompanha a forma **limitada** (CREST), em que a pele é acometida apenas na parte distal e o problema tardio típico é a hipertensão arterial pulmonar, e não a crise renal. Glicocorticoides em dose alta podem desencadear a crise renal.

questions.stem: A newborn girl is delivered at 38 weeks of gestation. Her heart rate is 52/min and regular. ECG shows P waves at a normal rate with no relationship to the QRS complexes. Echocardiography shows a structurally normal heart. Her 31-year-old mother had no prenatal care. She has had dry eyes and a dry mouth for 2 years. The mother has never had a facial rash, kidney disease or joint swelling. Which maternal antibody most likely caused the infant's condition?
questions.explanation: The infant has **congenital complete heart block** (AV dissociation) with a normal heart structure, a form of **neonatal lupus**. Maternal IgG **anti-Ro (SSA)**, often with anti-La (SSB), crosses the placenta and injures the fetal conduction system. The mother's dry eyes and mouth suggest **Sjögren syndrome**; mothers may also have SLE or no symptoms at all. Anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE, but it is not the antibody that causes congenital heart block.
questions.explanation_pt: O recém-nascido tem **bloqueio atrioventricular total congênito** (dissociação AV) com coração estruturalmente normal, uma forma de **lúpus neonatal**. O anticorpo IgG materno **anti-Ro (SSA)**, muitas vezes com anti-La (SSB), atravessa a placenta e lesa o sistema de condução fetal. O olho seco e a boca seca da mãe sugerem **síndrome de Sjögren**; a mãe também pode ter LES ou nenhum sintoma. O anti-dsDNA é altamente específico para LES, mas não é o anticorpo que causa o bloqueio cardíaco congênito.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a rash on his legs and buttocks for 3 days. Two weeks ago he had a sore throat and a runny nose. He has pain in both knees and ankles and has had episodes of crampy abdominal pain. The rash consists of raised purple spots that do not blanch and can be felt on palpation. Blood pressure is 102/64 mm Hg. Platelet count is 290,000/mm3, and PT and aPTT are normal. Urinalysis shows red blood cells and 1+ protein. A skin biopsy is done. Which finding is most likely?
choices: Hyaline platelet thrombi in small vessels without inflammation
Necrotizing inflammation of medium-sized arteries without immune deposits
Linear IgG deposits along the basement membrane
Leukocytoclastic vasculitis of small vessels with IgA deposits
questions.explanation: **Palpable purpura** on the legs and buttocks with normal platelets, arthralgia, abdominal pain and hematuria after a respiratory infection is **IgA vasculitis** (Henoch-Schönlein purpura), the most common vasculitis of childhood; it usually follows an infection by 1-3 weeks. **IgA immune complexes** deposit in the walls of small vessels and cause leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Pauci-immune vasculitis with granulomas (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) also involves small vessels and the kidney, but it has few or no immune deposits and usually affects adults with sinus and lung disease.
questions.explanation_pt: **Púrpura palpável** em membros inferiores e nádegas com plaquetas normais, artralgia, dor abdominal e hematúria após uma infecção respiratória é **vasculite por IgA** (púrpura de Henoch-Schönlein), a vasculite mais comum da infância; costuma surgir 1 a 3 semanas após uma infecção. **Imunocomplexos de IgA** depositam-se na parede de pequenos vasos e causam vasculite leucocitoclástica. A vasculite pauci-imune com granulomas (granulomatose com poliangiite) também acomete pequenos vasos e o rim, mas tem pouco ou nenhum depósito imune e costuma afetar adultos com doença sinusal e pulmonar.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man developed asthma 3 years ago, as an adult. He also has chronic nasal congestion with nasal polyps. One month ago he developed numbness and weakness of the right hand. For 1 week he has been unable to lift his left foot. Exam shows palpable purpura on both shins. Leukocyte count is 14,000/mm3 with 28% eosinophils. Chest x-ray shows patchy infiltrates that change location between films. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Adult-onset **asthma**, sinus disease, marked **eosinophilia**, migrating lung infiltrates and **mononeuritis multiplex** (two separate nerves) point to **eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis** (Churg-Strauss), a small-vessel vasculitis. When ANCA is present, it is usually **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis also affects the upper airway and lungs, but it is c-ANCA (anti-PR3) and lacks asthma and eosinophilia. Polyarteritis nodosa also causes mononeuritis multiplex, but it **spares the lungs**.
questions.explanation_pt: **Asma** de início na vida adulta, doença sinusal, **eosinofilia** acentuada, infiltrados pulmonares migratórios e **mononeurite múltipla** (dois nervos distintos) apontam para **granulomatose eosinofílica com poliangiite** (Churg-Strauss), uma vasculite de pequenos vasos. Quando há ANCA, geralmente é **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**. A granulomatose com poliangiite também acomete vias aéreas superiores e pulmões, mas é c-ANCA (anti-PR3) e não tem asma nem eosinofilia. A poliarterite nodosa também causa mononeurite múltipla, mas **poupa os pulmões**.

notes.title: Connective tissue diseases and vasculitis: antibodies and patterns
notes.body_md:
## Systemic lupus erythematosus

- Mostly young women. **Malar rash** that spares the nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis, serositis, cytopenias and nephritis.
- Immune complexes (**type III hypersensitivity**) consume complement: **low C3 and C4** in flares.
- **ANA** screens; **anti-dsDNA** and **anti-Smith** are specific.
- Linked topics: **lupus nephritis** (renal block), **Libman-Sacks endocarditis** (cardiology block), **antiphospholipid syndrome** (hemostasis block).
- **Drug-induced lupus**: **anti-histone**; hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid; resolves when the drug stops.

## Other connective tissue diseases

- **Sjögren syndrome**: dry eyes and mouth; **anti-Ro (SSA)** and **anti-La (SSB)**; risk of **MALT lymphoma**. Maternal anti-Ro can cause **congenital heart block**.
- **Systemic sclerosis**: limited (CREST) with **anti-centromere**; diffuse with **anti-Scl-70**, interstitial lung disease and **renal crisis**.
- **Dermatomyositis** and **polymyositis**: proximal weakness, high CK, sometimes **anti-Jo-1**. Dermatomyositis adds **heliotrope rash** and **Gottron papules** and calls for a search for cancer.
- **Mixed connective tissue disease**: **anti-U1 RNP**.

## Pain with normal strength

- **Polymyalgia rheumatica**: over 50, shoulder and hip stiffness, high ESR, normal CK; overlaps with giant cell arteritis.
- **Fibromyalgia**: widespread pain, fatigue, poor sleep, normal labs.

## Vasculitis by vessel size

- **Large**: **giant cell arteritis** and **Takayasu arteritis**.
- **Medium**: **polyarteritis nodosa** (hepatitis B, spares lungs), **Kawasaki disease** (coronary aneurysms) and **Buerger disease** (smokers).
- **Small, ANCA**: **granulomatosis with polyangiitis** (c-ANCA, anti-PR3), **microscopic polyangiitis** (p-ANCA, no granulomas), **eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis** (p-ANCA, asthma, eosinophilia).
- **Small, immune complex**: **IgA vasculitis** (Henoch-Schönlein purpura): children, palpable purpura, arthralgia, abdominal pain, hematuria.
- **Variable vessel**: **Behçet disease**: oral and genital ulcers, uveitis, HLA-B51.
- Drugs such as **hydroxychloroquine**, **methotrexate** and **rituximab** are covered in the musculoskeletal pharmacology block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Lúpus eritematoso sistêmico

- Principalmente mulheres jovens. **Eritema malar** que poupa os sulcos nasolabiais, fotossensibilidade, úlceras orais, artrite, serosite, citopenias e nefrite.
- Imunocomplexos (**hipersensibilidade tipo III**) consomem complemento: **C3 e C4 baixos** nas crises.
- O **FAN** (ANA) serve de triagem; **anti-dsDNA** e **anti-Sm** são específicos.
- Temas relacionados: **nefrite lúpica** (bloco renal), **endocardite de Libman-Sacks** (bloco de cardiologia), **síndrome antifosfolípide** (bloco de hemostasia).
- **Lúpus induzido por fármacos**: **anti-histona**; hidralazina, procainamida, isoniazida; regride com a suspensão do fármaco.

## Outras doenças do tecido conjuntivo

- **Síndrome de Sjögren**: olho seco e boca seca; **anti-Ro (SSA)** e **anti-La (SSB)**; risco de **linfoma MALT**. O anti-Ro materno pode causar **bloqueio cardíaco congênito**.
- **Esclerose sistêmica**: limitada (CREST) com **anticentrômero**; difusa com **anti-Scl-70**, doença pulmonar intersticial e **crise renal**.
- **Dermatomiosite** e **polimiosite**: fraqueza proximal, CK elevada, às vezes **anti-Jo-1**. A dermatomiosite acrescenta **eritema em heliotropo** e **pápulas de Gottron** e exige a busca de câncer.
- **Doença mista do tecido conjuntivo**: **anti-U1 RNP**.

## Dor com força normal

- **Polimialgia reumática**: acima de 50 anos, rigidez de ombros e quadris, VHS elevada, CK normal; sobrepõe-se à arterite de células gigantes.
- **Fibromialgia**: dor difusa, fadiga, sono ruim, exames normais.

## Vasculites pelo calibre do vaso

- **Grandes vasos**: **arterite de células gigantes** e **arterite de Takayasu**.
- **Médios vasos**: **poliarterite nodosa** (hepatite B, poupa os pulmões), **doença de Kawasaki** (aneurismas coronarianos) e **doença de Buerger** (tabagistas).
- **Pequenos vasos, ANCA**: **granulomatose com poliangiite** (c-ANCA, anti-PR3), **poliangiite microscópica** (p-ANCA, sem granulomas), **granulomatose eosinofílica com poliangiite** (p-ANCA, asma, eosinofilia).
- **Pequenos vasos, imunocomplexos**: **vasculite por IgA** (púrpura de Henoch-Schönlein): crianças, púrpura palpável, artralgia, dor abdominal, hematúria.
- **Vasos variáveis**: **doença de Behçet**: úlceras orais e genitais, uveíte, HLA-B51.
- Fármacos como **hidroxicloroquina**, **metotrexato** e **rituximabe** estão no bloco de farmacologia musculoesquelética.
